elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The clause states that “Licensor shall defend ... Licensee ... from and against any third-party claim.”

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer for damages, costs, and expenses resulting from covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Licensor must “indemnify and hold harmless Licensee” from the claim and “all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees).”

elements.element: Vendor's defense and indemnity must extend to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: The protected parties expressly include “Licensee and its affiliates.”

elements.element: Covered claims must be third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The operative grant expressly applies to “any third-party claim.”

elements.element: Covered claims must include allegations that the services or licensed technology infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The clause covers allegations that the “Licensed Technology ... infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right,” which is the operative equivalent of the supplied services subject in this licensing agreement.

elements.element: Covered claims must include allegations that deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The IP trigger expressly covers “any deliverable.”

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Subpart (b) covers “Licensor's breach of applicable law.”

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Subpart (c) covers “any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Licensee data caused by Licensor.”

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Subpart (d) expressly covers “Licensor's gross negligence.”

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Subpart (d) expressly covers “Licensor's ... wilful misconduct.”

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require prompt notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: The indemnified party must give the indemnifying party “prompt notice of the claim.”

elements.element: The indemnifying party must control the defense and settlement of the claim, subject to appropriate settlement protections.
elements.evidence: The indemnifying party controls “the defense and settlement,” and settlements imposing liability or an admission on the indemnified party require its consent.

elements.element: The indemnified party must provide reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: The indemnified party must provide “reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.”

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Article XII covers claims arising from “content or data provided by Licensee to Licensor.”

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover Customer's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Article XII covers “Licensee's breach of applicable law.”

elements.element: Customer's indemnity and related responsibility allocation must be limited exclusively to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Article XII retains a separate broad allocation making Licensee “solely responsible” for liability arising from its exercise of licensed rights and retains indemnity trigger (i) for “Licensee's exercise of any license or other rights.” It is therefore not limited to content and breach of law.

elements.element: Vendor must provide an intellectual-property indemnity in favor of Customer.
elements.evidence: Licensor expressly agrees to indemnify and hold harmless Licensee for the covered IP claim and resulting losses.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must cover third-party infringement claims involving the services or licensed technology.
elements.evidence: The clause covers a “third-party claim” alleging that the “Licensed Technology ... infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right.”

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must cover third-party infringement claims involving deliverables.
elements.evidence: The IP trigger expressly includes “any deliverable.”

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for modifications made by Licensee appears in the operative language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by combinations with items not supplied or approved by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combinations exclusion appears in the operative language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement resulting from Customer-provided specifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for compliance with Licensee specifications appears in the operative language.

elements.element: The IP remedies must permit Vendor to procure Customer's continued right to use the affected item.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no procure-right remedy.

elements.element: The IP remedies must permit Vendor to modify the affected item so that it becomes non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: The IP remedies must permit Vendor to replace the affected item with a non-infringing substitute.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: The IP remedies must require an applicable fee refund if procurement, modification, or replacement is unavailable or unsuccessful.
elements.evidence: No refund remedy appears, and the condition requiring a refund backstop is not demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Vendor's IP indemnity liability must be subject to a separate super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3× annual-fees super-cap appears. Instead, the indemnity applies “[n]otwithstanding Article XIII or any other provision,” taking it outside the existing one-half-of-fees cap without substituting the required super-cap.

result.reason: The Vendor-side indemnity and procedure substantially satisfy the preferred protections, but the preferred position fails because Licensee remains broadly responsible for, and must indemnify Licensor for, its exercise of licensed rights. That retained trigger can overlap with the new Licensor IP indemnity and create opposing indemnity obligations for the same infringement claim. The fallback also fails because none of the required modifications, combinations, or specifications exclusions, none of the procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and no 3× annual-fees super-cap are included. The redline is not minimal because it does not reach either complete level and uses an overbroad “notwithstanding ... any other provision” override while leaving the conflicting customer indemnity in place.
